turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Good morning.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm Dr. Siobhan Bayan. We met in the hospital back in February. Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Call it Mansur, September 8, 1967.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Mr. Mansur. The front desk mentioned you had a new insurance card.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, how we switched plans. The member ID is K, as in kilo -7 -3 -0 -9 -2 -5 -8.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Got it. I'll make sure they update it. So it's been about 8 months since your stent on February 11th. How are you doing overall? Heart -wise, good.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No chest pain at all since the stent. I finished cardiac rehab in June, and I'm walking 30 minutes most days.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's excellent. Any shortness of breath with the walking? No, I'm fine.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The kids at Roosevelt High School keep me moving too. I teach chemistry there.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Huh? That'll do it. Your portal message said you had a problem with the adorvastatin.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, so my thighs and calves were aching, both legs, like I'd run a marathon. It started maybe two months after the hospital. I put up with it, but about three weeks ago I just stopped taking it. I'm sorry, I know I should have called first.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No need to apologize, I'm glad you're telling me. What dose were you taking? 40 milligrams.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, wait, it's the big one.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 80 milligrams. Right, 80 is what we started in the hospital.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: And since you stopped it, how are the legs? much better maybe 90 % gone any muscle weakness trouble getting up from a chair or dark cola -colored urine know nothing like that good and the other medicines the aspirin clopidogrel and metaprolol you're still taking those aspirin 81 once a day clopidogrel 75 once a day and the metaprolol 25 milligrams once a day I haven't missed any of those great any bleeding or bruising on the two blood thinners. Some small bruises on my arms, nothing serious.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's common on those two, and you're still allergic to sulfa drugs.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, I get a rash all over.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, your blood pressure today is 124 over 76,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: pulse 62.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Heart has a regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs are clear. The spot on your right wrist where we put the catheter in is well -heeled. No tenderness in your thigh or calf muscles, goals, and your leg strength is normal. Good. Your labs from last week, so after about two weeks off the statin, show an LDL of 118. For someone with a stent, we want the LDL under 55, so that's well above goal. Your CK, the muscle enzyme, was normal at 145, and your liver tests were normal. So what now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I really don't want those aches back.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Totally understandable. muscle aches on statins are common and a lot of people do fine on a different statin at a lower dose. So I'd like to start Rasuvastatin 5 milligrams once a day and I'm adding Ezetimibe 10 milligrams once a day. It blocks cholesterol absorption in the gut and it doesn't cause muscle aches. Two new pills, huh? Yes, but together they should get you close to goal. If the aches come back stop the Rasuvastatin and send me a message but keep taking the esetimibe. Okay, that I can do. We'll recheck a lipid panel and liver tests in eight weeks. If your LDL is still above 55 after that, there are injectable cholesterol medicines we could talk about, but let's not get ahead of ourselves. Fair enough. Keep taking the aspirin and the clopidogrel through February, that's 12 months after the stent, and please don't stop the clopidogrel without talking to us first. Keep the metoprolol the same and keep up the walking. Well, do. So to sum up, you have coronary artery disease with a stent, which is stable and high LDL cholesterol, not at goal because you couldn't tolerate the atervastatin. I'll see you back in three months. Thanks,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Byan.
